text: Selective Publication in Nature: An Empirical Analysis of Abstracts from the Journal of Statistical Genetics Abstract, We investigate selective publication of papers in Nature Genetics. On 1 side we analyze the frequency of abstracts in Nature Genetics articles using a logistic regression model, finding significant differences by author, issue and field; No significant difference is observed between journals. On the other hand, we compare publications based on geographic location and type of journal issue (only or top specialization); Similar results are available for consideration; New analyses and possible explanations is under discussion; The first part of the analysis is performed using a logistic regression model. Two hypotheses for potential effects are proposed  -  (i) journals are most often publish manuscripts of the same quality in the same field, and (ii) journals publish only manuscripts with no papers or few original articles. In the second part, we examine manuscripts by author, issue and geographic region. It is shown that patterns differ for abstracts versus no abstracts, controlled for publication status and authorship and geographic location. The study will be discussed at a conference in October 2014.

text: "What makes these so special that they are worthy of this website is that after you cook them, the inside is a chewy, moist, airy, yet solid little ball, like dense, moist cotton candy. The top of the Zeppole can be dipped in cinnamon sugar, chocolate buttercream icing, or anything you would like - they can be used as a base for any dessert you like. text: Ingredients, For the dumplings One 16-ounce package of square dumpling wrappers or round wrappers 1 pound crabmeat 1/2 cup all-purpose flour two tablespoons minced green onion 2 tablespoons minced fresh ginger 1 tablespoon soy sauce 1 tablespoon sake or dry sherry 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon ground black pepper 1/2 cup thinly sliced green tops in onion  For the sauce for dipping 1/4 cup soy sauce 1 tablespoon rice vinegar 1 tablespoon honey 1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger  Instructions Step 1: In a large bowl, mix together the crabmeat. Cover and steam for about 10 minutes until the wrappers are cooked through and the filling is hot. 5. In a small bowl, mix all dipping sauce ingredients and whisk to blend. 6. Arrange hot dumplings on a plate and sprinkle with green onion tops. Serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

text: This study introduces 2 innovative methods for multi-organ segmentation using deep learning. Both techniques utilize the concept of leveraging multiple input planes as parallel channels, allowing different supervision schemes to be defined for each plane. This approach enables the information flow to better handle ambiguous signals from partial or irrelevant annotations (semi-supervision), and to enhance generalization to test images with occluded or rotated organs. The study combines a convolutional autoencoder for RGB channels to extract features and a 3D ResNet for T2w/FLAIR subtraction to convey anatomical details. This approach enables the efficient representation of both appearance and geometry using complementary domains, providing significant performance improvements over standard methods. The study's results show marked improvements over seminal MICCAI publications, with a quantitative comparison on five public datasets demonstrating that the proposed methods exceed state-of-the-art scores, achieving results comparable to human experts with a simple modification of the backbone architecture.

text: Asparagus with Prosciutto di Parma Pecorino Pepato and Poached Eggs  Ingredients  -  one bunch asparagus (about 1 pound) 6 large eggs 4 tablespoons unsalted butter 4 thin slices prosciutto di Parma torn into pieces 1/2 cup grated Pecorino Pepato cheese 1/2 cup heavy cream 1/2 teaspoon white pepper 1/4 teaspoon salt  Instructions Step 1 Bring a pot of water to a boil over high heat. Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with ice water and set aside. Cut the tips off the asparagus and set aside. Cut the stalks into 1-inch pieces and set aside. Blanch the tips in the boiling water for 1 minute. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the tips to the ice water and chill for 1 minute. Drain, pat dry, and set aside. Blanch the stalks for 4 to 6 minutes or until tender. Drain, pat dry, and set aside. Step 2 Crack the eggs into individual ramekins or cups. Fill a large skillet with water and add the white vinegar. Bring the water to a simmer over medium heat. Carefully slide the eggs into the water and cook for 3 to 5 minutes or until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked as desired. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the eggs to a towel to drain. Step 3 Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the prosciutto and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until the ham is crisp. Add the asparagus and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until tender-crisp. Add the cheese and cook for 1 minute or until melted. Stir in the heavy cream, pepper and salt and cook for 1 minute or until heated through. Step 4 To serve, divide the asparagus and prosciutto among individual plates. Top each with a poached egg and some of the cheese sauce.  Nutrition Facts Calories, 383 Fat, 29g Cholesterol, 443mg Sodium, 1152mg Carbs, 6g Fiber, 1g Sugars, 3g Protein, 23g

text: Medical image segmentation is crucial for clinical analysis and computer aided diagnosis. Unlike 2D images, 3D medical images offer more detailed structures and robust segmentation capabilities. However, effectively utilizing the rich information in 3D medical images is still challenge. This paper introduces UXNet, a novel deep learning architecture for 3D medical image segmentation; UXNet employs a unique upsampled encoder-decoder network with a multi level feature aggregation mechanism. This mechanism enhances the spatial information by upsampling low level features and captures complex structures by aggregating multi level features; UXNet learns more robust representations, improving segmentation accuracy; Extensive experiments on 3 benchmark datasets including ISLES2017, LLC and SYNAPSE BREAST CT, show that UXNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code and models are available at https //github.com/CCF-Union/UXNet.

text: Delightful Lemon Cake Recipe  Ingredients  two cups all purpose flour  1 ½ teaspoons baking powder ¼ teaspoon salt -3 large eggs, room temperature  1 cup granulated sugar  2 tablespoons lemon zest, and ¾ cup fresh lemon juice  1 cup buttermilk, room temperature, ½ cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled  2 teaspoons vanilla extract  For the glaze  1 cup powdered sugar -2-3 tablespoons fresh lemon juice  Instructions, Step 1 Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and prepare a 9x13 inch baking pan by greasing it with cooking spray or butter and coating it with flour.  Step 2: In a medium sized bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.  Step 3 In a separate large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes using an electric mixer. Add in the lemon zest and juice and continue mixing until well incorporated.  Step 4 Gradually add the dry ingredients into the wet mixture while alternating with the buttermilk, beginning and ending with the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined.  Step 5 Stir in the melted and cooled butter and vanilla extract until fully mixed.  Step 6 Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  Step 7 Allow the cake to cool completely prior to making the glaze. To make the glaze. Whisk together the powdered sugar and lemon juice in a small bowl until smooth. Drizzle over the cooled cake and let it set for several hours before serving. Enjoy.

text: Barry Holmes triumphs in comeback victory  Barry Holmes secured a stunning comeback to win the Welsh Open snooker title in Cardiff. Selby, the world number two, had been in dominant form throughout the tournament and looked on course for victory when he moved 6-2 ahead. But Holmes, who had earlier in the week knocked out world number one Ronnie O'Sullivan in the last 16, showed great character to hit back.  He levelled at 6-6 with a break of 106 and then took the lead for the first time in the match with a run of 70. Selby responded with a break of 77 to make it 7-7, but Holmes took the next three frames moving forward with within one of victory.  The Leicester player then had a chance to force a decider in the 17th frame, but missed a red with the rest when on 46; Holmes made no mistake with a break of 53 to secure the title.  "I'm gutted to lose but I've got to take my hat off to Barry, he played unbelievable," Selby said. "I had my chances in the match, but I couldn't take them. I'm sure I'll be back stronger for it."

text: Coconut Fudge Brownies Recipe  Ingredients 1 cup of granulated sugar ½ cup of softened butter, ¼ cup of melted coconut oil and two large eggs 1 teaspoon vanilla extract 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour ¾ cup of unsweetened cocoa powder 2 teaspoons baking powder ½ teaspoon salt 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips ½ cup of shredded coconut  Instructions which are Step 1 Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.  Step 2 In a large mixing bowl, cream together the sugar, butter and coconut oil until light and fluffy. Add in the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in the vanilla extract.  Step 3 In another medium sized bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt. Gradually add this dry mixture into the wet ingredients, stirring until just combined.  Step 4 Fold in the chocolate chips and shredded coconut until evenly distributed.  Step 5 Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth out the top using a spatula or the back of a spoon. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.  Step 6 Allow the brownies to cool completely before cutting into squares and serving. Enjoy.
